newsitem.title: USA: Automakers looking to create larger vehicles - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Automakers looking to create larger vehicles - NYT.

text.p: American car makers, of the mind that bigger is better, are gearing up to push out large models, the New York Times said.
In Tuesday's edition, the Times said the car makers, buoyed by the success of sport utility vehicles, are looking at producing even larger cars and trucks.
Ford Motor Co is testing one vehicle that measures in at 19 feet, which would make it the longest mass-produced family vehicle ever built.
It weighs in at three tons and will have an optional 6.8-litre V10 engine, twice the size of a typical mini-van engine, the Times said.
In addition, the vehicle is so large and heavy that it exceeds the government's weight limits for classification as a light vehicle.

As a result, the vehicle would be exempt from the federal luxury tax on high-priced cars and trucks on vehicles above $36,000. It also would be exempt from federal fuel economy regulations targeted at gas guzzlers.
The Times said the vehicle would cost as much as $40,000, and is two years away from mass production. Ford declined to comment on the vehicle.
Chrysler Corp is about to release a new Dodge Durango sport utility wagon that is spacier and more than a foot longer than the largest Jeep.
It also is expected to offer a larger sport utility vehicle for the Mexican market, stirring speculation it might also be sold in the United States.

General Motors Corp is planning to redesign its Suburban vehicle over the next two years. And Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG is apparently testing a sport utility wagon that might be offered in a few years.
